subject.title: fix(browser): stop screenshot vision-failure fallback from injecting raw base64

question: When a configured image-understanding model fails for `browser screenshot`, should OpenClaw retain this PR’s text-only failure/share result, or should it provide a session-safe model-visible image recovery path?
rationale: Both outcomes are plausible product behavior: the proposed path prevents session contamination but deliberately removes the prior fallback during a provider failure, so source review and test proof cannot determine the intended user recovery contract.

options.title: Accept text-only recovery
options.body: Approve the PR’s scoped contract: report the configured-vision error as text and require an explicit message-tool share for the staged screenshot.

options.title: Design safe image recovery
options.body: Keep this PR open for a follow-up design that restores image recovery without retaining base64 image blocks in recent session context.

recommendation.title: Accept text-only recovery
recommendation.body: Approve the PR’s scoped contract: report the configured-vision error as text and require an explicit message-tool share for the staged screenshot.

likelyOwner.reason: The only identifiable contributor in the supplied review context can clarify the proposed contract and incorporate the owner decision; browser-area ownership should be confirmed by a human reviewer.
